binary 0dceb07e (seat 28 planted build).why: Same as 1a9460d6: second planted control, hash recorded, no recipe.

dataset digest e6beb5f9 (bench SUM over.why: A sha256 over a per-position result table (i|fen|nodes|score|best), not a build identifier. It resolves trivially because it is a checksum OF A RESULT, and is listed only so it is not mistaken for a build. It does not itself pin a build: two different builds can disagree and both be internally consistent, so a row resting ONLY on this digest still needs its build named. That is a gap in those rows, recorded below.

named PC r15 (label).why: The LABEL resolves through the committed handoff: PC r15 = 6b98f217 + FABLE_TO_swarm_5.md patch = binary 068f0927. Both halves verified (patch sha256 and rebuilt binary sha256). A label is resolved when the record pins it to an artefact that exists, which this one does.

branch handoff/fable-opus-combo29-all.why: origin/handoff/fable-opus-combo29-all-20261114 exists (4bf72522a..64620a554). Same tree family as integrate/combo29-all; not the audit base.

\"the owner's PC\" (net not shared).why: The handoff states the PC plays with its own trained net which is explicitly NOT shared, and that cloud seats keep the built-in evaluation. So any row whose value depends on the owner's net is not reproducible by anyone outside that machine, by design. Rows that say 'no net file' / 'built-in eval' are unaffected; rows that quote the PC's own strength numbers are.

It is a settings block applied to a build, not a build. It is listed so that a reader does not count it as a build identifier; it resolves trivially because it is just a list of setoption commands.

binary ae1a49b6 (PC r15 ASan+UBSan).why: The ASan+UBSan build of PC r15 (35 __asan_ / 15 __ubsan_ symbols reported). No recipe recorded: the reports name the flags only as 'ASan+UBSan'. I tried three standard flag sets on the rebuilt r15 source (address,undefined; +-g; +-O1 -g) and got 1bc76c68 / 830e178d / d6222004 -- none is this hash. The SANITIZER RESULT does not depend on the exact bytes (a sanitizer finding is about what the instrumented build DID, and the source is reproducible), but the hash itself cannot be re-derived, so a reader cannot prove they are holding the same instrument.

binary 581159a4 (seat 01 -D_GLIBCXX_DEBU.why: A -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG build used as a control. My -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG build of the base gave 715b7c90, not this hash. No recipe recorded beyond the single flag, so some other flag differs and the record does not say which.

binary 698d2d9b (PC r15 TSan).why: A ThreadSanitizer build of PC r15. No recipe recorded; TSan builds are highly sensitive to flags, so this is the least reproducible class in the set.

descriptor: ASan+UBSan build (flags neve.why: The report says 'ASan+UBSan build' and never records the flag set, the compiler line or a hash. Sanitizer findings are about BEHAVIOUR, so the claim usually survives without the bytes -- but it cannot be replicated, and an ASan build that differs in optimisation still detects the same defect. Treat these rows as behavioural evidence, not as reproducible measurements. Distinct from b109a0a5, which is the one ASan build that did get a hash (and still no recipe).

descriptor: TSan build (flags never reco.why: 'TSan build' with no flag set and no hash (one row names 698d2d9b for the r15 TSan build; the rest name nothing). TSan builds are the most flag-sensitive in the set. 27 findings use the descriptor, 1 uses the hash; both are unresolvable.

descriptor: -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG build (flag.why: Named only by the single flag. My -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG base build gave 715b7c90 against a reported 581159a4, so at least one other flag differs and the record does not say which. Small blast radius (2 findings, one seat).
